category: Particle Tracing Module II: forces, collisions, particle heat and mass, bidirectional study and particle results
description: Forces acting on particles (drag laws, lift, Brownian, gravity, thermophoresis, dielectrophoresis, magnetophoresis, acoustophoresis, electric and magnetic Lorentz forces, friction), Monte Carlo collisions with a background gas and particle-matter interactions in Charged Particle Tracing, particle heat/mass/charge features of Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow (heat losses, droplet breakup and evaporation, charge accumulation), field-accumulating domain features, the Bidirectionally Coupled Particle Tracing study, and particle-specific datasets, derived values and plots (Particle Bin, Particle Evaluation, Phase Portrait, Poincare Map, trajectory filters, beam variables). Type strings verified against COMSOL 6.4 completion data.

tools.name: Drag Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Exerts the fluid drag on particles using a selectable drag law: Stokes (default, Re_p << 1), Oseen correction, Schiller-Naumann (Re_p up to about 800), Haider-Levenspiel (nonspherical particles via sphericity), Hadamard-Rybczynski (clean bubbles and droplets) or Standard drag correlations (piecewise fits over a wide Re range). Options add wall corrections, rarefaction (Cunningham-Millikan-Davies, Basset, Epstein, Phillips), virtual mass and pressure gradient forces and turbulent dispersion.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Drag Force (df1); API: physics("fpt").create("df1", "DragForce", 3); set("DragLaw", "Stokes"|"SchillerNaumann"|"OseenCorrection"|"HaiderLevenspiel"|"HadamardRybczynski"|"StandardDragCorrelations")

parameters.name: DragLaw
parameters.description: Drag correlation; with 'Newtonian, ignore inertial terms' Stokes drag is always used.

parameters.name: u / u_src
parameters.description: Fluid velocity: user-defined components or taken from a flow interface (Common model input).

parameters.name: mu_mat / rho_mat
parameters.description: Fluid viscosity and density from material or user defined.

parameters.name: IncludeWallCorrections / Rarefaction_Effects
parameters.description: Near-wall Stokes corrections; slip correction model when rarefaction is enabled on the interface.

parameters.name: IncludeVirtualMassAndPressureGradientForces
parameters.description: Adds added-mass and pressure-gradient terms (important for bubbles).

parameters.name: TurbulentDispersionModel
parameters.description: NoneTurbulenceModel | DiscreteRandomWalk | ContinuousRandomWalk (needs k and epsilon/omega).

tools.notes: Required for Fluid-Particle Interaction, Volume Force Calculation and Droplet Breakup. Small particles force small time steps with Newtonian formulations (relaxation time ~ rho_p d_p^2 / 18 mu).

tools.name: Lift Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Applies a lift force on particles moving through a nonuniform (sheared) creeping flow, using either the Saffman law (particles far from walls) or the Wall induced law that accounts for two parallel walls on either side of a parabolic channel profile. It is the key force for inertial focusing and pinched-flow fractionation in microfluidics.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Lift Force (lf1); API: physics("fpt").create("lf1", "LiftForce", 3); set("LiftLaw", "Saffman"|"WallInduced")

parameters.name: LiftLaw
parameters.description: Saffman (default) or WallInduced (select Parallel Boundary 1 and 2).

parameters.name: u, rho, mu
parameters.description: Fluid velocity, density and viscosity (from material or flow interface).

tools.notes: Only with Newtonian or Newtonian first order formulations. The wall-induced law is expensive in 3D because the nearest wall point is searched every step.

tools.name: Brownian Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Adds a random force at every time step that reproduces Einstein diffusion of suspended particles from the fluid temperature and viscosity. It matters mainly for submicron particles (aerosols, nanoparticles) and makes trajectories stochastic, so results are usually averaged over many particles or Monte Carlo runs.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Brownian Force (bf1); API: physics("fpt").create("bf1", "BrownianForce", 3)

parameters.name: Temperature T (model input)
parameters.description: Fluid temperature.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity
parameters.description: From material, flow interface or user defined.

parameters.name: Additional input argument to random number generator
parameters.description: With interface RandomNumberArgs = UserDefined, sweep this argument for independent realizations.

tools.notes: Adding the force clears 'Update scaled absolute tolerance' in the time-dependent solver so the solver does not chase the noise; use a fixed maximum step for reproducible statistics.

tools.name: Gravity Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Applies gravity and, by specifying the surrounding fluid density, buoyancy to particles. The gravity vector defaults to g_const along -y (2D) or -z (2D axisymmetric and 3D) and can point in any direction with any magnitude.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Gravity Force (gf1); API: physics("fpt").create("gf1", "GravityForce", 3)

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Gravity vector (default 0, 0, -g_const in 3D).

parameters.name: Density (fluid)
parameters.description: From material or user defined; enables buoyancy.

parameters.name: Particles to affect
parameters.description: All, single species or logical expression (ei).

tools.notes: For submicron particles drag and Brownian forces usually dominate and gravity can be omitted.

tools.name: Thermophoretic Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Moves particles down temperature gradients in a gas (thermophoresis), important for soot, aerosol deposition on cold walls and semiconductor contamination. With rarefaction effects enabled the model can be Epstein (continuum), Waldmann (free molecular), Talbot or Linearized BGK (wide Knudsen range); otherwise the Epstein model is used.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Thermophoretic Force (thpf1); API: physics("fpt").create("thpf1", "ThermophoreticForce", 3); set("ThermophoreticForceModel", "Talbot")

parameters.name: ThermophoreticForceModel
parameters.description: Epstein | Waldmann | Talbot (default) | LinearizedBGK.

parameters.name: T, pA (model inputs)
parameters.description: Gas temperature field and absolute pressure.

parameters.name: mu_mat / k_mat / Cp_mat
parameters.description: Gas viscosity, thermal conductivity and heat capacity.

parameters.name: MeanFreePathCalculation
parameters.description: IdealGasHardSphereCollisions | UserDefinedCorrection.

tools.notes: Needs the temperature from a heat transfer interface; enable 'Include rarefaction effects' on the interface to access all force models.

tools.name: Dielectrophoretic Force / Shell (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Applies the dielectrophoretic (DEP) force on neutral particles in a nonuniform electric field, driven by the permittivity (and, for AC fields, conductivity) contrast between particle and fluid via the Clausius-Mossotti factor; particles move toward higher field norm when more polarizable than the fluid. Shell subnodes model layered particles such as biological cells with membranes.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Dielectrophoretic Force (deff1); right-click > Shell (shl1); API: physics("fpt").create("deff1", "DielectrophoreticForce", 3); feature("deff1").create("shl1", "Shell", 3)

parameters.name: SpecifyForceUsing
parameters.description: ElectricField (default) or ElectricPotential, from Electrostatics/Electric Currents (stationary or frequency domain).

parameters.name: epsilonr / sigma
parameters.description: Fluid relative permittivity and electric conductivity.

parameters.name: AngularFrequency / omega
parameters.description: FromSolution or UserDefined angular frequency for AC DEP.

parameters.name: Shell: ts, ers, sigmas
parameters.description: Shell thickness, relative permittivity and conductivity per layer.

tools.notes: Particle permittivity and conductivity are entered in Particle Properties. The force depends on gradients of |E|^2, so use quadratic or higher discretization or piecewise polynomial recovery.

tools.name: Magnetophoretic Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Applies the force on magnetizable particles in a nonuniform magnetic field arising from the permeability contrast between particle and fluid, used for magnetic bead separation and magnetic drug targeting. Particles are treated as homogeneous spheres; the force depends on spatial derivatives of the magnetic field H.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Magnetophoretic Force (mpf1); API: physics("fpt").create("mpf1", "MagnetophoreticForce", 3)

parameters.name: H
parameters.description: Magnetic field (user defined or from Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents).

parameters.name: mur
parameters.description: Fluid relative permeability (>= 1); particle relative permeability is set in Particle Properties.

tools.notes: With vector-potential formulations the needed derivatives of H may be unavailable; use piecewise polynomial recovery or a scalar-potential formulation.

tools.name: Acoustophoretic Radiation Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Applies the time-averaged acoustic radiation force on small particles (Rayleigh limit) in a harmonic acoustic field computed in a Frequency Domain study, as used in acoustofluidic particle sorting and acoustic levitation. Solid particles or liquid droplets are supported with Ideal, Viscous or Thermoviscous loss models; microstreaming is not included.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Acoustophoretic Radiation Force (acof1); API: physics("fpt").create("acof1", "AcoustophoreticForce", 3)

parameters.name: ParticleType
parameters.description: SolidParicle (solid particle, default) or LiquidDroplet.

parameters.name: ThermodynamicLossModel
parameters.description: Ideal | Viscous | Thermoviscous (needs more fluid and particle properties).

parameters.name: pA / uaco / freq
parameters.description: Acoustic pressure, acoustic velocity and frequency (FromSolution by default).

parameters.name: Fluid properties
parameters.description: rho, c (speed of sound), mu, muB, kcond, Cp, alphap, gammash.

tools.notes: Solve Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain first, then trace particles in a Time Dependent step that references that solution.

tools.name: Electric Force (Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Applies the electric part of the Lorentz force qE to charged particles, with the field given as an electric field or as the gradient of an electric potential. The field may be stationary/time dependent, time harmonic (frequency from the solution or user defined, with initial phase) or periodic with a user-defined period and time shift, which is how RF quadrupoles and ion traps are modeled.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing (or Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow) > Electric Force (ef1); API: physics("cpt").create("ef1", "ElectricForce", 3)

parameters.name: SpecifyForceUsing
parameters.description: ElectricField (E) or ElectricPotential (V), user defined or from es/ec/emw.

parameters.name: TimeDependenceOfField
parameters.description: StationaryOrTimeDependent | TimeHarmonic | Periodic (Tper, dtper).

parameters.name: FrequencySpecification / omega / phi0
parameters.description: FromSolution | SpecifyFrequency | SpecifyPeriod; initial phase angle.

parameters.name: Particles to affect
parameters.description: All, single species or logical expression.

tools.notes: Newtonian formulations only. Piecewise polynomial recovery improves field accuracy on coarse meshes. Existing entry 'Drag Force / Electric Force / Magnetic Force (particle forces)' gives a combined overview.

tools.name: Magnetic Force (Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Applies the magnetic part of the Lorentz force q v x B, curving particles without changing their energy. B can be user defined, taken from a magnetic field interface, time harmonic or periodic, or set to Earth's magnetic field from built-in geomagnetic data using particle positions or a geographic location (city or latitude/longitude/altitude and epoch 1950-2015).
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Magnetic Force (mf1); API: physics("cpt").create("mf1", "MagneticForce", 3); set("B", ...) or set("B_src", "EarthsMagneticField")

parameters.name: B / B_src
parameters.description: Magnetic flux density: userdef, a physics interface, or EarthsMagneticField.

parameters.name: LocationSpecification / LocationDefinedBy / City / lat / lon / alt / epoch
parameters.description: Geomagnetic field options: FromParticlePositions or GeographicLocation.

parameters.name: TimeDependenceOfField
parameters.description: StationaryOrTimeDependent | TimeHarmonic | Periodic.

tools.notes: Energy drift in pure magnetic motion indicates too loose solver tolerances; tighten the relative tolerance or use the first-order Newtonian formulation.

tools.name: Collisions (Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Parent node for Monte Carlo collisions between model particles and a rarefied background gas defined by number density, molar mass, temperature and (optionally drifting) velocity. At each solver step, or with the null-collision method at random times, the collision probability is computed from cross sections or collision frequencies of the subnodes (Elastic, Excitation, Attachment, Ionization, Resonant and Nonresonant Charge Exchange, User Defined).
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Collisions (col1); subnodes via right-click; API: physics("cpt").create("col1", "Collisions", 3)

parameters.name: Nd / mg / T / u
parameters.description: Background number density (default 1e20 1/m^3), molar mass (0.04 kg/mol), temperature (293.15 K), velocity.

parameters.name: CollisionDetection
parameters.description: AtTimeStepsTakenBySolver | NullCollisionMethodColdGasApproximation.

parameters.name: CountAllCollisions
parameters.description: Adds an auxiliary counter of all collisions per particle.

parameters.name: Accumulator subnode
parameters.description: Collect collision-driven quantities in domain elements.

tools.notes: For a deterministic, averaged drag use Friction Force instead. Collisions producing new particles need 'Maximum number of secondary particles'.

tools.name: Elastic (Collisions subnode, Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Momentum-conserving elastic collision between model particles and background gas molecules, specified by a collision cross section (constant or energy-dependent interpolation) or directly by a collision frequency. Particles similar in mass to the gas thermalize quickly to a Maxwellian; very light particles (electrons) keep non-Maxwellian distributions.
tools.usage: Right-click Collisions > Elastic (ela1); API: physics("cpt").feature("col1").create("ela1", "Elastic", 3)

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: CrossSection (xsec, default 3e-19 m^2) or CollisionFrequency (nu, default 2e6 Hz).

parameters.name: NumberDensitySpecification / MolarMassSpecification
parameters.description: FromParent or UserDefined (Nd, mg).

parameters.name: CountCollisions
parameters.description: Count collisions of this type per particle.

tools.notes: In 2D axisymmetry with out-of-plane DOFs set the cutoff radial coordinate rcop to avoid singular behavior near the axis.

tools.name: Excitation / Attachment (Collisions subnodes, Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Inelastic collision types for electrons in a background gas: Excitation removes a fixed energy loss per collision (electronic or vibrational excitation), while Attachment captures the incident electron on a gas molecule, optionally releasing the resulting negative ion as a new particle species. Both are typically combined with Elastic and Ionization subnodes to build a complete electron-gas reaction set.
tools.usage: Right-click Collisions > Excitation (exc1) / Attachment (att1); API: feature("col1").create("exc1", "Excitation", 3) / create("att1", "Attachment", 3)

parameters.name: Specify / xsec / nu
parameters.description: Cross section or collision frequency.

parameters.name: dE (Excitation)
parameters.description: Energy loss per collision.

parameters.name: ReleaseAttachedParticle / ReleasedIonProperties (Attachment)
parameters.description: Release the negative ion and choose its Particle Properties node.

tools.notes: Cross-section tables vs energy are typically imported as interpolation functions (for example LXCat data).

tools.name: Ionization (Collisions subnode, Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Electron-impact ionization of the background gas with a given energy loss (typically 12-24 eV): the primary electron continues, a secondary electron is released and the created ion can optionally be released as a third particle. It enables Monte Carlo avalanche, multiplication and ion-source models.
tools.usage: Right-click Collisions > Ionization (ion1); API: physics("cpt").feature("col1").create("ion1", "Ionization", 3)

parameters.name: dE
parameters.description: Ionization energy loss.

parameters.name: ReleasePrimaryElectron / ReleaseSecondaryElectron / ReleaseIonizedParticle
parameters.description: Which particles continue or are created (defaults: on, on, off).

parameters.name: ReleasedElectronProperties / ReleasedIonProperties
parameters.description: Particle Properties nodes used for the released electron and ion.

tools.notes: Preallocate enough secondary particles on the interface; runaway avalanches quickly exhaust the budget.

tools.name: Resonant / Nonresonant Charge Exchange (Collisions subnodes, Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Charge-exchange collisions of ions with background atoms: Resonant Charge Exchange (same species, no internal energy change) and Nonresonant Charge Exchange (different species, with energy loss and optional change of the primary ion species). The fast neutral, the slow ion, or both can be released, which is essential for ion beam neutralization and charge-exchange cells.
tools.usage: Right-click Collisions > Resonant Charge Exchange (cex1) / Nonresonant Charge Exchange (ncex1); API: feature("col1").create("cex1", "ResonantChargeExchange", 3) / create("ncex1", "NonResonantChargeExchange", 3)

parameters.name: SpeciesToRelease
parameters.description: Ion | Neutral | IonAndNeutral.

parameters.name: chis
parameters.description: Scattering angle in the center-of-mass system (default 0).

parameters.name: dE / ChangePrimaryIonSpecies (Nonresonant)
parameters.description: Energy defect and whether the primary becomes another species.

parameters.name: ReleasedNeutralProperties / ReleasedIonProperties
parameters.description: Particle Properties for released particles.

tools.notes: Charge exchange cross sections are often much larger than elastic ones at low energy.

tools.name: User Defined collision / Species Properties (Collisions subnode, Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Generic collision type in which the post-collision velocity of the primary particle is given by an arbitrary expression, with optional release of additional species described by Species Properties subnodes. Use it for collision processes not covered by the built-in types, such as custom scattering distributions or detachment.
tools.usage: Right-click Collisions > User Defined (udi1); right-click User Defined > Species Properties (spp1); API: feature("col1").create("udi1", "UserDefined", 3)

parameters.name: Specify / xsec / nu
parameters.description: Cross section or collision frequency.

parameters.name: vr
parameters.description: Reinitialized particle velocity after the collision.

parameters.name: ReleasePrimaryParticle
parameters.description: Keep (1) or remove (0) the primary particle.

tools.notes: Use random() in vr expressions for stochastic angular distributions.

tools.name: Friction Force (Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Deterministic alternative to Monte Carlo collisions that represents momentum loss to a background gas as a drag proportional to the relative velocity, using a collision-frequency equation (cross section and number density, or collision frequency) or the Mason-Schamp equation for ion mobility. Velocities change smoothly, allowing larger time steps than stochastic collisions.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Friction Force (ff1); API: physics("cpt").create("ff1", "FrictionForce", 3)

parameters.name: SpecifyForceUsing
parameters.description: CollisionFrequencyEquation | MasonSchampEquation.

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: CrossSectionAndNumberDensity (xsec, Nd) | CollisionFrequency (nu).

parameters.name: u / T / mg
parameters.description: Background velocity, temperature and molar mass (Mason-Schamp).

tools.notes: Suited for ion mobility spectrometers and ion funnels at moderate pressure where individual collisions need not be resolved.

tools.name: Particle-Matter Interactions / Ionization Loss / Nuclear Stopping (Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Models energetic ions penetrating solid material: the parent node sets target density, atomic mass and number, projectile atomic number, cutoff energy and absorbed-dose accumulators; Ionization Loss applies continuous electronic stopping (Protons on silicon, Alpha particles on silicon or user-defined stopping power) and Nuclear Stopping applies Monte Carlo nuclear scattering with Bohr, Moliere, Lenz-Jensen or Universal screening. Typical uses are ion implantation ranges and radiation dose.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Particle-Matter Interactions (pmi1) > Ionization Loss (il1) / Nuclear Stopping (ns1); API: physics("cpt").create("pmi1", "ParticleMatterInteractions", 3); feature("pmi1").create("il1", "IonizationLoss", 3); feature("pmi1").create("ns1", "NuclearStopping", 3)

parameters.name: rho / Am / Zm / Zp
parameters.description: Target density, atomic mass (default 28.0855 u), atomic number (14) and projectile atomic number.

parameters.name: StopBelowCutoff / Ec
parameters.description: Stop particles below the cutoff energy (default 8.6 eV).

parameters.name: AbsorbedDose / AbsorbedDoseFromIonizationLosses / AbsorbedDoseFromNuclearStopping / Qf
parameters.description: Accumulated dose variables and quality factor.

parameters.name: ElectronicStoppingPower / Se (Ionization Loss)
parameters.description: ProtonsOnSilicon | AlphaParticlesOnSilicon | UserDefined.

parameters.name: ScreeningFunction / chic (Nuclear Stopping)
parameters.description: NoneScreeningFunction | Bohr | Moliere | LenzJensen | Universal; cutoff scattering angle (default 0.1 deg).

tools.notes: At least one subnode is required. A larger cutoff scattering angle skips weak nuclear collisions and allows larger time steps.

tools.name: Space Charge Density Calculation (Charged Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Domain feature that defines an accumulated dependent variable for the space charge density of the particles (and optionally their current density) without automatically feeding it back to a field interface. Use it to inspect beam charge distributions or to build custom couplings; for automatic bidirectional coupling use the Electric Particle Field Interaction multiphysics node.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Space Charge Density Calculation (scd1); API: physics("cpt").create("scd1", "SpaceChargeDensityCalculation", 3)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Charge multiplication factor (Specify release times; default 1e6 real particles per model particle).

parameters.name: ComputeCurrentDensity
parameters.description: Also accumulate the current density vector.

tools.notes: With Specify current the charge accumulates over the elements each particle has traversed, which represents a steady beam.

tools.name: Number Density Calculation (Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Domain feature that counts particles per mesh element and divides by the element volume (area in 2D, revolved volume in 2D axisymmetry) to give a particle number density field, optionally with the element-averaged particle velocity. The count can be restricted to one release feature or species and scaled by a number multiplication factor.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing / Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Number Density Calculation (ndc1); API: physics("fpt").create("ndc1", "NumberDensityCalculation", 3)

parameters.name: nn
parameters.description: Number multiplication factor (Specify release times, default 1).

parameters.name: ComputeAverageVelocity
parameters.description: Also compute the mean velocity of particles in each element.

parameters.name: Particle selection
parameters.description: Release feature or Particle Properties restriction.

tools.notes: Elementwise constant result; statistical noise decreases with more particles per element.

tools.name: Volume Force Calculation (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Domain feature that defines dependent variables for the volume force exerted by particles on the fluid (equal and opposite to the drag in each element), computed like the Fluid-Particle Interaction coupling but without automatically adding it to the flow equations. Use it to assess whether two-way coupling is needed or to apply the force manually.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Volume Force Calculation (vfc1); API: physics("fpt").create("vfc1", "VolumeForceCalculation", 3)

parameters.name: Force multiplication factor specification
parameters.description: From physics or User defined (Specify release times).

tools.notes: Requires at least one Drag Force node.

tools.name: Convective Heat Losses / Radiative Heat Losses / Heat Source (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Particle heat balance features available when 'Compute particle temperature' is enabled: Convective Heat Losses exchanges heat with the surrounding fluid via a heat transfer coefficient or a Nusselt correlation, Radiative Heat Losses applies Stefan-Boltzmann exchange with a particle emissivity, and Heat Source adds a user-defined power per particle (e.g. chemical reaction or induction heating). Particle temperature is assumed uniform (Biot number << 1).
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Convective Heat Losses (chl1) / Radiative Heat Losses (rhl1) / Heat Source (hts1); API: physics("fpt").create("chl1", "ConvectiveHeatLosses", 3); create("rhl1", "RadiativeHeatLosses", 3); create("hts1", "HeatSource", 3)

parameters.name: Heat source definition (Convective)
parameters.description: Specify heat transfer coefficient (h, default 10 W/(m^2*K)) or Specify Nusselt number (default).

parameters.name: Particle emissivity (Radiative)
parameters.description: Default 1.

parameters.name: Q (Heat Source)
parameters.description: Heat source per particle in W.

tools.notes: Particle specific heat is taken from Particle Properties. Add Dissipated Particle Heat to return the exchanged heat to the fluid.

tools.name: Dissipated Particle Heat (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Domain accumulator that collects the heat exchanged between particles and fluid through Convective and Radiative Heat Losses into a volumetric heat source or sink for the carrier fluid, so that a Heat Transfer in Fluids interface can be two-way coupled to the particle temperatures. User Heat Source nodes are not included.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Dissipated Particle Heat (dph1); API: physics("fpt").create("dph1", "DissipatedParticleHeat", 3); use the accumulated variable as Heat Source Q in ht

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Only input; the accumulated variable is elementwise constant.

tools.example: fpt > Dissipated Particle Heat dph1 on all domains; Heat Transfer in Fluids > Heat Source with Q0 = the dph1 accumulated variable (pick it from the expression list), then solve fpt and ht together to verify energy conservation.
tools.notes: Requires 'Compute particle temperature' on the interface.

tools.name: Droplet Breakup (Kelvin-Helmholtz / Rayleigh-Taylor models)
tools.description: Models secondary atomization of liquid droplets: the Kelvin-Helmholtz Breakup Model strips small child droplets from a parent (coefficient B_KH, default 10) and the Rayleigh-Taylor Breakup Model shatters rapidly accelerating droplets completely (coefficient C_RT, default 5). Child droplets are released as secondary particles, limited per breakup when macroparticles are used.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Droplet Breakup (dr1) with subnodes Kelvin-Helmholtz Breakup Model (kh1, default) and Rayleigh-Taylor Breakup Model (rt1); API: physics("fpt").create("dr1", "DropletBreakup", 3); feature("dr1").create("rt1", "RayleighTaylor", 3)

parameters.name: Prerequisites
parameters.description: Newtonian formulation, particle mass or diameter solved for, Liquid droplets/bubbles type, Drag Force in the same domains.

parameters.name: B_KH / C_RT
parameters.description: Model coefficients of the Kelvin-Helmholtz and Rayleigh-Taylor models.

parameters.name: Nmax
parameters.description: Maximum number of model particles released per breakup (macroparticles, default 10).

parameters.name: Gas properties
parameters.description: Gas density and velocity field for the KH model.

tools.notes: Only one subnode of each type per Droplet Breakup node. Set the interface 'Maximum number of secondary particles' high enough for all child droplets.

tools.name: Droplet Evaporation (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Computes the rate of droplet mass loss by evaporation into the surrounding gas using the diffusive Maxwell model, the Stefan-Fuchs model (includes Stefan flow) or a user-specified evaporation constant, optionally coupled with droplet heating. Droplets below a cutoff mass or diameter are removed.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Droplet Evaporation (evap1); then select it in Particle Properties > Accretion or evaporation rate specification; API: physics("fpt").create("evap1", "DropletEvaporation", 3)

parameters.name: EvaporationModel
parameters.description: Maxwell (default) | StefanFuchs | SpecifyEvaporationConstant (kappav).

parameters.name: SaturationVaporPressure / pvs / pvref / Tref
parameters.description: ClausiusClapeyronEquation or UserDefined vapor pressure at the droplet surface.

parameters.name: VaporDiffusionCoefficient / Dv / pva / Mv
parameters.description: Vapor diffusivity, ambient vapor pressure and vapor molar mass.

parameters.name: IncludeDropletHeating / RemovalofSmallDroplets
parameters.description: Coupled heating; Never | SpecifyCutoffParticleMass (mpc) | SpecifyCutoffParticleDiameter (dpc).

tools.notes: Only valid when the particle mass or diameter is a dependent variable (Specify particle mass/diameter).

tools.name: Charge Accumulation (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Solves for the charge acquired over time by particles immersed in a gas containing free ions (electrostatic precipitators, aerosol chargers), using Lawless, Classical diffusion, Classical field, Classical diffusion and field, or White charging models. The accumulated charge number then drives Electric Force on the particles.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Charge Accumulation (cacc1); API: physics("fpt").create("cacc1", "ChargeAccumulation", 3)

parameters.name: T / p
parameters.description: Gas temperature and pressure (for ion mobility from the reduced mobility muiN).

parameters.name: Particle charging model
parameters.description: Lawless (default) | Classical diffusion | Classical field | Classical diffusion and Field | White.

parameters.name: Zai
parameters.description: Initial accumulated charge number (default 0).

parameters.name: ParticleElectricalProperties / SpecifyElectricFieldUsing / rhoq
parameters.description: Dielectric or Conductive particles; field from E or V; ion space charge density.

tools.notes: Couple with Electrostatics (space charge from a corona model) and an Electric Force node.

tools.name: Bidirectionally Coupled Particle Tracing (study step)
tools.description: Study step for self-consistent coupling between particles and stationary fields: it generates a For/End For loop that alternates a Time-Dependent solver for the particle degrees of freedom and a Stationary solver for the fields (potential, flow), iterating a fixed number of times or until a global variable converges. Use it for constant-current beams with space charge and constant-mass-flow fluid-particle interaction instead of an expensive fully transient solve.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Time Dependent > Bidirectionally Coupled Particle Tracing; API: model.study("std1").create("bcpt", "BidirectionallyCoupledParticleTracing")

parameters.name: tlist
parameters.description: Output times for the particle trajectories.

parameters.name: Termination method
parameters.description: Fixed number of iterations (default 5) or Convergence of global variable (relative tolerance 0.001, min/max iterations).

parameters.name: usertol / rtol
parameters.description: User-defined relative tolerance of the time-dependent solver (default 0.01).

tools.notes: Requires Specify current (cpt) or Specify mass flow rate (fpt) so that each particle represents a steady flux. Pulsed or transient fields need a fully coupled Time Dependent study instead.

tools.name: Particle Bin (dataset)
tools.description: Dataset that groups particles into bins by the value of an expression (limits, number of bins with equal count or equal width, or a tolerance for discrete values) and replaces each bin by one averaged macroparticle. Plots and evaluations using the bin dataset then show averaged trajectories, for example the mean path of each particle size class.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > More Datasets > Particle Bin (pbin1), input = a Particle dataset; API: model.result().dataset().create("pbin1", "ParticleBin")

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Binning expression, e.g. fpt.dp.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: limits | number (default, with distribution equalnumber or equalwidth) | tolerance.

parameters.name: number / limits / tolerance
parameters.description: Bin settings for the chosen method.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module.

tools.name: Particle Evaluation (derived value)
tools.description: Derived value that evaluates an expression for every particle (or a fraction or number of them) at the selected output times of a Particle dataset, returning a table with one column per particle. Use it to export particle energies, positions or auxiliary variables for post-analysis.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > More Derived Values > Particle Evaluation (par1); API: model.result().numerical().create("par1", "Particle"); getReal()

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression(s) evaluated on each particle.

parameters.name: evaluate
parameters.description: all | fraction (fraction) | number (number of particles).

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A Particle dataset.

tools.notes: For global statistics (averages, fractions) prefer Global Evaluation of particle-counter or status variables.

tools.name: Phase Portrait (plot)
tools.description: 2D plot for large particle datasets in which each particle is a dot at (position, speed) by default, or at any two user-defined expressions (for example transverse position vs transverse velocity to visualize beam emittance ellipses). Color Expression subnodes add a third quantity.
tools.usage: 2D Plot Group > More Surface Plots > Phase Portrait; API: model.result("pg1").create("phpo1", "PhasePortrait")

parameters.name: x-axis
parameters.description: Position (distance from origin) or Manual expression.

parameters.name: y-axis
parameters.description: Speed or Manual expression.

tools.notes: Normalize the two axes to similar magnitudes for a readable plot. Requires the Particle Tracing Module.

tools.name: Poincare Map (plot)
tools.description: Plot that places a dot wherever a particle trajectory crosses a cut plane (first-recurrence map), reducing trajectories by one dimension; a particle can cross the plane many times. It is used to study mixing quality, chaotic advection, periodic orbits and beam cross sections.
tools.usage: Create a Cut Plane dataset on the Particle dataset, then 3D (or 2D) Plot Group with data = cut plane > More Volume/Surface Plots > Poincare Map; API: model.result("pg1").create("poma1", "PoincareMap")

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A Cut Plane dataset defined on a Particle dataset.

parameters.name: fixedpointsize / pointradiusexpr / sphereradiusscale
parameters.description: Dot size settings.

tools.notes: Available with the Particle Tracing Module, 3D trajectories only.

tools.name: Filter (Particle Trajectories subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of a Particle Trajectories plot that restricts which particles are drawn: All, Primary, Secondary, or those satisfying a logical expression (for example a Particle Counter's <tag>.rL or cpt.Ep>1[keV]), and optionally only a fraction or a fixed number of them. It keeps plots of millions of particles responsive and highlights subsets.
tools.usage: Right-click Particle Trajectories > Filter (filt1); API: model.result("pg1").feature("traj1").create("filt1", "ParticleTrajectoriesFilter")

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: all | primary | secondary | logical (logicalexpr).

parameters.name: evaluate
parameters.description: all | fraction (fraction) | number (number).

tools.notes: Combine with a Particle Counter so only transmitted particles are shown.

tools.name: Particle Tracing / Particle Tracing with Mass (plots)
tools.description: Core COMSOL postprocessing plots (no Particle Tracing Module needed) that integrate pathlines of massless particles in a computed velocity field, or of particles with mass under a user-defined force, directly from a Solution dataset. Particles can be released once, at intervals or at given times and drawn as lines, tubes, points, comet tails or arrows.
tools.usage: 2D/3D Plot Group > More Point Plots > Particle Tracing (ptr1) or Particle Tracing with Mass; API: model.result("pg1").create("ptr1", "Particle") / create("ptrm1", "ParticleMass")

parameters.name: expr / fx, fy, fz / mass
parameters.description: Velocity field (massless) or force components and particle mass (with mass).

parameters.name: xcoord / ycoord / zcoord
parameters.description: Release positions.

parameters.name: dropmethod
parameters.description: once | freq (dropfreq) | times (droptimes).

parameters.name: linetype / pointtype / pointdom
parameters.description: Line or tube rendering; point, comet tail or arrow markers; stick or disappear at boundaries.

tools.notes: These plots do not feed back to the model and support only simple forces; use the Particle Tracing Module interfaces for walls, releases and forces. Mass must not be time dependent.

tools.name: Particle beam variables (emittance, Twiss parameters, hyperemittance)
tools.description: Global variables defined when a Particle Beam release is present: 1-rms and 4-rms transverse emittances, Twiss parameters alpha, beta and gamma for each transverse direction, 3D hyperemittance, and the beam average position and velocity, all computed relative to the beam centroid and mean direction. Plot them versus time to follow beam divergence, focusing and emittance growth through lenses.
tools.usage: Evaluate in Results > Global Evaluation / 1D Global plot on the particle solution; browse them with Replace Expression under Charged Particle Tracing > Particle beam (names are prefixed by the interface and feature scope, e.g. cpt.pbeam1.*)

parameters.name: Emittance (1-rms / 4-rms)
parameters.description: Area measures of the transverse phase-space ellipse.

parameters.name: Twiss alpha, beta, gamma
parameters.description: Ellipse shape parameters (Courant-Snyder: beta*gamma - alpha^2 = 1).

parameters.name: Average position / velocity
parameters.description: Beam centroid used to define transverse coordinates.

tools.example: Particle Beam pbeam1 on the source aperture; 1D Plot Group > Global with the beam's 4-rms emittance expression (from Replace Expression) over time shows emittance growth in an einzel lens (Application Library: einzel_lens).
tools.notes: Exact variable names depend on the feature tag and transverse direction; insert them via the expression browser rather than typing.

tools.name: Particle size distribution and macroparticles (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Additional Variables settings of Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow that decide whether particle size is fixed (Uniform size) or solved for as mass or diameter per particle (needed for evaporation, breakup and accretion), and whether each model particle is a macroparticle representing many physical particles through a multiplication factor. Initial sizes can be sampled from distributions in the release features.
tools.usage: Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Settings > Additional Variables > Particle size distribution (UniformSize | SpecifyParticleMass | SpecifyParticleDiameter), Enable macroparticles; release node > Initial Particle Mass / Diameter and Initial Multiplication Factor sections

parameters.name: ParticleSizeDistribution
parameters.description: UniformSize | SpecifyParticleMass | SpecifyParticleDiameter.

parameters.name: Enable macroparticles
parameters.description: Adds a multiplication factor per particle (required by Nozzle).

parameters.name: Initial size distribution (release)
parameters.description: A list of diameters or sampled from the built-in normal, lognormal (count median diameter CMD and geometric standard deviation GSD) or uniform distributions.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("fpt").prop("ParticleSizeDistribution").set("ParticleSizeDistribution", "SpecifyParticleDiameter");
// in Inlet inl1: Initial Particle Diameter section -> sample from a lognormal distribution
tools.notes: Particle Bin datasets are a convenient way to postprocess by size class.

tools.name: Random number generation and Monte Carlo runs (Particle Tracing)
tools.description: Stochastic particle features (Brownian force, diffuse wall scattering, collisions, random releases, probabilistic wall conditions) use seeded random numbers so repeated solves give identical results. The interface setting Arguments for random number generation (Generate unique arguments, Generate random arguments, User defined) plus each feature's Additional input argument let you run independent realizations, for example with a Parametric Sweep over the argument.
tools.usage: Particle interface > Advanced Settings (Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options) > Arguments for random number generation; feature > Advanced Settings > Additional input argument to random number generator (property i)

parameters.name: RandomNumberArgs
parameters.description: GenerateUnique (default, reproducible) | GenerateRandom | UserDefined.

parameters.name: i
parameters.description: Additional input argument per feature (UserDefined mode).

tools.notes: Keep reproducible seeding for verification; randomize only for ensemble statistics.
